summary: Multiplexed batch: client cancel + handoff leads to missing tool acknowledgements on retry
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that when their orchestrator multiplexes multiple user sessions into a single persistent streaming connection, a client-side cancel + handoff (client cancels locally and another process replays the session) results in the serving layer issuing a retry but the downstream tool webhook does not receive or acknowledge the second attempt, causing missing side effects.

Impact:
- Intermittent lost webhook side effects (order creations) for ~0.2% of requests during high concurrency.
- Customer (BrightDocs.ai) sees user-facing missing confirmations and manual reconciliation load.

Environment:
- Dedicated cluster in us-east, reserved GPU pool.
- Use of TypeScript SDK v1.14.2 with multiplexing enabled; orchestrator written in Python (sdk-python v0.9.8).
- Model: redwood/llama-2-13b-quant pinned.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Start 300 concurrent sessions multiplexed over 10 streams.
2) For a subset of sessions the client intentionally cancels the request mid-stream and the orchestrator replays session from persisted queue.
3) The SDK emits a client-side CANCEL event and immediately attempts a handoff replay on a new connection.
4) Serving runtime logs show a retry/redirect to another worker instance.
5) Downstream tool webhook (order service) reports no second POST; first POST sometimes succeeded but invoice/receipt webhook missing.

Expected behavior:
- Retries should reach the downstream tool once and be deduplicated by idempotency key; the tool should receive the retried invocation or the system should surface a clear failure that prevents silent loss.

Actual behavior:
- In ~0.2% of runs the retried invocation appears never to arrive at the webhook endpoint. No 5xx error from serving. No explicit 2xx ack on second attempt.

Logs / artifacts included:
- Customer attached orchestrator logs and a pcap of the client-side handoff sequence (sensitive redacted).
- Serving trace IDs: trace:us-east:20260310:7a3b9c (sampled).

Additional notes:
- Customer suspects an edge case where connection migration + client-cancel race causes the idempotency header to be dropped or rewritten during handoff.
- They also note that Python orchestrator uses persistent background workers which may reuse ephemeral session salts.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:15 - Miguel Santos (Support): Acknowledged receipt and requested full trace IDs and the orchestration replay code sample. Asked for sample webhook logs and whether the webhook endpoint returned 4xx/5xx at any time.
2026-03-10 11:02 - BrightDocs.ai (Customer): Uploaded orchestration snippet + selected pcap. Confirmed webhook returns 200 on first attempt; no record of second attempt in the order service logs.

2026-03-10 14:30 - Lina Chen (SRE): Reproduced approximate pattern in staging with smaller load. Observed that when client cancels while a stream chunk is in-flight and a retry is scheduled, the multiplexer stripped a custom header 'x-rw-idempotency' due to per-connection header normalization before proxying to the worker. Filed a short-term hypothesis: header normalization in the edge sidecar may drop non-standard headers during mid-stream connection handoff.

2026-03-11 09:00 - Eng (runtime): Confirmed a code path in our HTTP/2 sidecar that rebuilds request metadata on connection migration and did not copy over 'x-rw-idempotency' when the original connection had been canceled. Created PR to add idempotency header preservation and added integration test to simulate cancel+replay.

2026-03-11 13:45 - Support (Miguel): Shared suggested customer workaround: include idempotency key within the JSON funcall payload (application-level fallback) and patch orchestrator to persist that key per session before canceling. This is not ideal but prevents silent loss.

2026-03-12 16:00 - BrightDocs.ai (Customer): Implemented application-level idempotency and reported a drop to 0.01% missing cases; awaiting runtime patch to revert workaround. Asked about timeline and rollout constraints for dedicated clusters.

2026-03-12 18:20 - Lina Chen (SRE): Noted PR reference and deployment plan for dedicated customers; hotfix scheduled for next maintenance window. Advised customer that Dedicated clusters will receive the patch in their planned minor release; private deployments will get guidance for a config toggle in sidecar (preserve_custom_headers_on_migration=true).
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Edge sidecar normalizes headers on connection migration and may drop non-standard headers => missing idempotency header on retry.
Hypothesis 2: Multiplexer or SDK layer may re-generate session salts leading to idempotency key mismatch across replayed connection.
Hypothesis 3: Background worker process reuse (Python) may race with per-request nonce generation causing truncated/absent header when canceled mid-chunk.

Staging test: Created synthetic harness that cancels at chunk boundaries and asserts header presence. Found missing header in 1/500 runs matching customer rate. Root cause traced to sidecar header copy logic.
resolution: Workaround provided: persist idempotency key in funcall payload and keep that persisted across client cancel/handoff until replay completes. Engineering fix: sidecar update to preserve custom idempotency headers during connection migration. PR merged and hotfix scheduled for dedicated clusters in next minor release. Customer confirmed significant reduction after app-level workaround and will validate after hotfix rollout. Follow-up: Add e2e integration test for cancel+replay path and update SDK docs with guidance on 'idempotency in payload' pattern for multiplexing use cases.
